summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive, data-driven planetary atlas developed to identify and compare potential Earth analog environments for future Moon and Mars exploration missions.

Addressing the challenge of finding reliable terrestrial analog sites, TerraTwin goes beyond visual similarities to evaluate measurable terrain characteristics. Using NASA and USGS datasets, the platform analyzes parameters such as slope distribution, local relief, and terrain ruggedness to compare planetary reference locations with candidate environments on Earth.

At its core, TerraTwin features the Terrain Analog Similarity Index (TASI), a transparent multi-criteria scoring model that helps users assess and rank potential analog sites. It highlights locations such as Egypt's Western Desert and Gilf Kebir, turning complex geospatial data into accessible interactive maps and comparisons.

By supporting more informed site selection and realistic pre-mission testing, TerraTwin aims to reduce engineering uncertainty and help prepare safer, more reliable planetary exploration missions.
details:
TerraTwin – Detailed Project Description

1. Project Overview

TerraTwin is an interactive planetary atlas designed to help researchers and mission planners identify and evaluate potential terrestrial analog environments for future Moon and Mars exploration missions.

The project addresses a major challenge in planetary exploration: an Earth location may visually resemble the surface of Mars or the Moon without sharing the physical terrain characteristics required for realistic rover testing and mission preparation. TerraTwin replaces subjective visual comparisons with a structured, data-driven approach to terrain analysis.

2. How the Platform Works

TerraTwin combines planetary and terrestrial geospatial datasets to compare selected reference locations with potential Earth analog sites.

Its main workflow consists of four stages:

A. Scientific Data Integration

The platform uses NASA and USGS geospatial resources, including Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) elevation products, NASA Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) elevation data, and relevant thermal datasets where available.

B. Terrain Analysis

Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are processed to extract measurable terrain characteristics, including:

  • Slope Distribution: Evaluates the steepness and distribution of terrain gradients.
  • Local Relief: Measures elevation variation within a defined neighborhood.
  • Terrain Ruggedness: Characterizes surface elevation variability and roughness.

C. Terrain Analog Similarity Index (TASI)

TerraTwin introduces an experimental, transparent multi-criteria scoring model called the Terrain Analog Similarity Index (TASI).

The model combines normalized terrain metrics using the following proposed weighting scheme:

  • Slope Distribution: 40%
  • Local Relief: 35%
  • Terrain Ruggedness: 25%

The resulting score provides a comparative indication of terrain similarity between a planetary reference site and an Earth candidate location. It is intended as a decision-support metric rather than a definitive scientific validation of an analog site.

D. Interactive Geospatial Visualization

Users can explore candidate locations, inspect terrain information, compare locations, and view analytical results through an interactive mapping interface.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

TerraTwin aims to make planetary analog research more accessible, transparent, and reproducible.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Supporting the identification of promising terrestrial environments for rover mobility experiments and equipment testing.
  • Reducing reliance on subjective visual similarity when selecting analog sites.
  • Helping researchers identify terrain mismatches before conducting field experiments.
  • Highlighting scientifically interesting terrestrial environments, including Egypt's Western Desert.
  • Making complex planetary and geospatial information easier to explore through an interactive interface.

Ultimately, TerraTwin aims to support better-informed mission preparation and reduce engineering uncertainty before future planetary exploration missions.

4. Creativity and Innovation

The central innovation of TerraTwin is its shift from appearance-based analog selection to quantitative terrain comparison.

Rather than simply displaying images of deserts and planetary surfaces, the platform combines geospatial data processing, measurable terrain characteristics, and a transparent scoring methodology in one interactive environment.

The TASI framework also makes the comparison process easier to understand by showing how different terrain characteristics contribute to the overall similarity score.

The project further emphasizes Egypt's potential contribution to planetary analog research by bringing attention to its desert environments as candidates for future scientific investigation.

5. Factors Considered

The team considered several factors when designing the comparison methodology:

  • Terrain slope and elevation variability.
  • Local topographic relief.
  • Surface ruggedness and terrain complexity.
  • Spatial resolution and compatibility between datasets.
  • Data quality, missing values, and measurement limitations.
  • The importance of transparent calculations and reproducible comparisons.

We recognize that terrain similarity alone cannot establish complete environmental equivalence. Soil composition, mineralogy, atmospheric conditions, thermal behavior, and mechanical properties require additional datasets and dedicated analysis.

6. Technology and Development Tools

The project uses a combination of web development technologies and scientific computing tools.

Frontend:

  • React and TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Leaflet / React-Leaflet for interactive maps
  • Recharts for analytical visualizations

Backend and Scientific Processing:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • NumPy and Pandas
  • Rasterio
  • SciPy

Geospatial Data:

  • NASA MOLA elevation products
  • NASA SRTM elevation data
  • Relevant NASA thermal datasets
  • USGS geological and terrestrial reference resources

The platform is designed as a browser-based application to make its maps, comparisons, and analytical results accessible without specialized desktop GIS software.

7. Current Implementation and Future Development

The current project focuses on its delivered Mars-to-Earth terrain comparison capabilities, including interactive mapping, terrain metric analysis, and the TASI scoring framework, to the extent implemented in the submitted version.

Future development plans include integrating NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data for lunar polar terrain analysis, expanding mineralogical and multispectral comparisons, and incorporating additional environmental and mechanical parameters.

These improvements would extend TerraTwin from a terrain-focused comparison platform into a more comprehensive planetary analog research tool.
